aarti.pad1: With the Gaṅgā on his head and Pārvatī as half his body, the dweller of Kailāsa is ever enthroned. Nandī and Bhṛṅgī dance, and the gods meditate on him, the treasury of happiness. ॥1॥
aarti.pad2: A cool, gentle, fragrant breeze blows; there sits Śiva, the imperishable. The gandharvas sing in the seven notes, rāgas and rāgiṇīs of the sweetest kind. ॥2॥
aarti.pad3: Where yakṣas, rākṣasas and bhairavas roam, and the dwellers of the forest call; the cuckoo sounds its lovely note, and the bees make a humming. ॥3॥
aarti.pad4: Kalpa trees and pārijāta trees grow there by the lakh; where crores of wish-granting cows roam, as though raining milk. ॥4॥
aarti.pad5: The mountain shines like the sunstone, the masses of snow like the moonstone. All six seasons are ever lovely there, and Nature, as a maidservant, always serves. ॥5॥
aarti.pad6: Seers, sages, gods and dānavas serve him daily; the Vedas sing of him, the treasury of virtues. Brahmā and Viṣṇu gaze at him night and day, thinking: Śiva will give us some command. ॥6॥
aarti.pad7: Śiva is the giver of ṛddhi and siddhi, ever the treasury of being, consciousness and bliss; the moment one remembers him, the hard noose of Death and Yama is cut. ॥7॥
aarti.pad8: Whoever sings the name of the trident-bearer constantly and with love, that man's troubles are removed, and birth after birth he will reach Śiva's feet. ॥8॥
aarti.pad9: Dweller of Kailāsa, dweller of Kāśī, imperishable one, take care of me. Knowing me always the servant of your feet, knowing me your own, show me mercy. ॥9॥
aarti.pad10: You, my Lord, are ever merciful; cover all my failings. Forgive every offence, Śiva, and hear the plea of your servant. ॥10॥
